articleTitle: Laser pointing angle measurement for the geoscience laser altimeter
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A laser pointing angle measurement system developed for the geoscience laser altimeter has been environmentally tested and is in compliance with its 7.3 urad error budget over expected spaceflight temperature variations.

abstract: We have demonstrated a novel scheme to generate watt-level of mid-IR output with intracavity periodically poled RbTiOAsO/sub 4/ (PPRTA) OPOs pumped by a diode-pumped Nd:YALO laser. Outputs of 0.66 W at 3.73 /spl mu/m and 2.13 W at 1.5 /spl mu/m with 39.4 /spl mu/m PPRTA, and 1.7 W of 2 /spl mu/m for 41.95 /spl mu/m PPRTA were achieved.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Semiconductor saturable absorbers are monolithically integrated with large area high-index-contrast AlGaAs/Al/sub x/O/sub y/ broadband mirrors. The mirrors are used to self-start and mode-lock a Cr:Forsterite laser generating 30 fs pulses.

articleTitle: Beatwave acceleration of 12 MeV electrons to 50 MeV using shaped CO/sub 2/ laser pulses
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A plasma heatwave accelerator with a gradient /spl sim/1.3 GeV/m is presented. It is shown that for diffraction limited plasmas, when efficiency of the plasma wave excitation is restricted by ionization-induced refraction, acceleration of electrons is enhanced by using asymmetric, long pulses.

articleTitle: Midinfrared coherent sources using enhanced nonlinear frequency conversion in isotropic semiconductors
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Tunable midinfrared sources (8-12 /spl mu/m) based on GaAs and ZnSe slabs are presented. Quasi-phase matched difference frequency generation is obtained by total internal reflection. In nanosecond operation, we get up to 0.5 nanojoule of midinfrared light.

articleTitle: Three-dimensional terahertz holography
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate three-dimensional terahertz (THz) holography with the use of the windowed Fourier transformation. The coherent nature of THz time domain spectroscopy allows measurement of the phase and amplitude of the THz wave for holographic imaging.

articleTitle: Dispersion of two-photon absorption coefficient for a CdS-ZnO nanocomposite thin film using antiresonant ring interferometer
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We discuss the dispersion of two-photon absorption coefficient for a CdS-ZnO nanocomposite thin film using a new, sensitive, simple and single beam technique called antiresonant ring interferometric spectroscopy.

articleTitle: E-band fiber Raman amplifier in nonzero dispersion fiber
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An E-band fiber Raman amplifier in nonzero dispersion fiber is demonstrated with a 39 dB peak gain. Gain fiber water absorption is not observed to significantly hinder amplification. Such a device could extend the telecommunications bandwidth.

articleTitle: Generation of 9-fs 5-mJ pulses using a hollow fiber with pressure gradient
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We have demonstrated the generation of 9-fs 5-mJ pulses at 800 nm using spectral broadening by self-phase modulation in a hollow fiber with pressure gradient and dispersion compensation by chirped mirrors.

articleTitle: Coupled-mode and FDTD analysis of transverse Bragg resonance (TBR) waveguides
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A coupled-mode approach to analysing a transverse Bragg resonance (TBR) waveguide is compared to a two dimensional finite difference time domain calculation. We show the coupled-mode formalism can provide an intuitive method to analyse TBR waveguides even for large index contrasts.

articleTitle: Assessment of the optical phase jitter in dispersion-managed systems
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

articleTitle: Prototype front end for a petawatt laser system using optical parametric chirped-pulse amplification
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A highly efficient, prototype optical parametric chirped-pulse-amplification (OPCPA) system has been built as the front end for a petawatt laser system operating at 1053 nm. The design details and measured performance will be presented.

articleTitle: Self-referencing carrier-envelope offset beats and widely tunable sub-30 fs pulses from a compact Er:fiber laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An ultrabroadband frequency comb is generated by a novel Er:fiber system and characterized with an f-to-2f scheme. Clean maxima in the spectrum are tuned between 1100 nm and 1400 nm and compressed to pulse widths of 26 fs.

articleTitle: Spectral two-photon absorption in the range of 1.3-1.75 /spl mu/m for GaAs
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: For the first time we have measured the spectrum of two-photon absorption coefficient for GaAs based on Z-scan technique. We have observed a peculiar feature in the spectrum and compared our results with the two previous discrete values.

articleTitle: High power hybrid laser with an optical parametric oscillator and gaseous amplifiers
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A novel hybrid laser chain, called SOFIA (solid-state oscillator followed by iodine amplifiers), with a commercial solid state optical parametric oscillator and gaseous narrow-linewidth iodine amplifiers (1315.24 nm) is presented. The laser will pump the optical parametric chirped pulse amplification.

articleTitle: Demonstration of monolithic optical injection locking using a two section DFB laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A simplified monolithic optical injection locking system using a two section DFB laser is demonstrated. The operating wavelength of the two sections is current tuned to achieve optical injection locking; when locked the modulation bandwidth is increased from 10 GHz to 23 GHz.

articleTitle: Intentionally-induced pre-PMD for suppression of nonlinear effects in 16/spl times/40 Gb/s WDM repeaterless transmission systems over 225 km of SMF
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Nonlinear-effects suppression by a pre-PMD scheme was confirmed in a WDM system, for the first time. An average Q factor-budget improvement of 0.4 dB was demonstrated in 16-channel 43 Gb/s CS-RZ repeaterless transmission experiments over 225 km SMF.

articleTitle: Thermal characteristics of GaAs-based quantum cascade lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We have investigated the thermal dynamics in GaAs-based quantum cascade lasers during pulsed operation with an interferometric thermal mapping technique. The method enables us to determine thermal properties of these multilayered structures.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

articleTitle: Functional THG microscopy with plasmon-resonance enhancement in silver nanoparticles
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Functional third-harmonic-generation (THG) microscopy is proposed/demonstrated by labeling the samples with silver nanoparticles. Over 100-fold THG enhancement can be observed by coinciding the signal frequency with the surface-plasmon-resonance frequency of <50-nm silver nanoparticles.

articleTitle: Spatially-resolved velocity profile measurements by means of a two-wavelength technique
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A measuring system based on a differential laser-Doppler anemometer has been extended to determine one-dimensional velocity profiles of shear flows with a spatial resolution in the micrometer range. The principle of the realised velocity profile sensor is based on two-wavelength fringe systems with different gradients of their fringe spacings. After wavelength-sensitive detection two Doppler frequencies are determined, which yield the position as well as the velocity component of individual tracer particles.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate generation of 3.7-fs pulses with energies up to 15 /spl mu/J through adaptive compression of the supercontinuum output of a cascaded hollow fiber by a spatial light modulator.

articleTitle: Temperature profile measurement in high power optical fiber components using a distributed fiber sensor
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate a new method for measuring temperature distribution changes caused by coupling a high power laser beam into a multimode fiber and by splicing of two multimode fibers. The measurement technique is based on interrogating a distributed sensor implemented using a fiber Bragg grating.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

articleTitle: High-energy short-pulse diode-pumped Nd:YVO/sub 4/ laser and its applications for material sciences and biomedical imaging
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate a very inexpensive high-energy picosecond laser oscillator, which is easy to maintain and to use for variety of applications ranging from pulsed laser deposition to advanced biomedical imaging. The described system should be also capable for efficient pumping of high-energy parametric oscillators and even parametric amplifiers to produce broadly tunable high-energy sub-picosecond IR pulses. Picosecond high-power diode-pumped solid state lasers are particular important because of their numerous applications in medicine and material processing.

articleTitle: Shock-shells in Coulomb explosion of nano-clusters
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Coulomb explosion of a gas cluster invariably produces shocks of infinite density; a pair of shocks forms a shock-shell that eventually encompasses the entire cluster. This first example of nm-size shock waves promises several new effects, including nuclear reactions inside exploding clusters.

articleTitle: Novel technologies for high-brightness AlGaInP LEDs
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The III-V semiconductor system AlGaInP is today the only material suitable for the fabrication of high-brightness LEDs in the yellow to red color range. In this paper, we will compare a number of new approaches for high-brightness LEDs, including the thin-film technology. The discussion will include the potential of various approaches as well as their benefits and drawbacks.

articleTitle: Carrier confinement in 1300-nm InGaAsN quantum-well lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Theoretical and experimental analysis of carrier transport in high-performance 1300-nm InGaAsN QW lasers, indicate significant thermionic hole leakage. Experimental optimization of the InGaAsN QW lasers by suppressing the carrier leakage, results in an extremely-low threshold current density of only 440 A/cm/sup 2/ at temperatures of 90/spl deg/C.

articleTitle: 40 cm size multilayer dielectric gratings for LULI laser pulse compressor
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A pair of 420/spl times/210 mm size multilayer dielectric gratings has been produced to equip the laser pulse compressor at LULI, to double the output power (in replacement of gold coating gratings). A review of performances is presented.

articleTitle: Femtosecond micromachining of symmetric active waveguides by astigmatically shaped beams
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We present a novel astigmatic beam shaping technique to fabricate, by femtosecond laser pulses, waveguides with circular transverse profile and arbitrary size. We obtain single-mode active waveguides at 1.5 /spl mu/m with gain of 1.5 dB.

This system consists of three major components; a 600 mJ seeded 2.05-micron pump laser, a ZnGeP/sub 2/ parametric oscillator and amplifier and a cw periodically poled lithium niobate seed source for parametric oscillator.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The effect of the split ratio on bandwidth enhancement for two-contact lasers is investigated experimentally. It is found that with a split ratio of 7:1, a bandwidth enhancement of 36% is achieved.

abstract: We report an optically pumped surface-emitting semiconductor laser which is passively mode-locked and generates 1.9 W of average power in 27-ps pulses at 0.96 /spl mu/m. The maximum diffraction-limited continuous-wave output is 4.4 W.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Parametric amplifiers can boost signals with 0 dB noise-figure penalty, which for conventional linear optical amplifiers approaches 3 dB at high gains. We will present results on noise performance of fiber optical parametric amplifiers, focusing on regimes of noiseless signal amplification.

abstract: We present a statistical model for studying migration assisted upconversion processes in high-concentration erbium-doped fiber amplifiers. Obtained theoretical results agree experimental data for a small signal gain at 1530 nm.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A new pulse shaping technique was developed for maximizing the energy of /spl sim/1 /spl mu/s pulses amplified in a double cladding fiber amplifier. Stimulated Brillouin scattering was avoided; the nearly square amplified pulses reached 20 /spl mu/J energy.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate optical pulse sequence generation at rates of 100 Gb/s using a novel direct space-to-time pulse shaping technique. The pulse sequences are generated by parallel-to-serial conversion of the spatial profile of the short input pulse to the pulse shaper.

articleTitle: Optimization of pulse regeneration by self-phase modulation in fibers
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We investigate the effects of fiber length, launch power, and filter offset on the performance of an all-fiber 2R regenerator based on self-phase modulation. Experimental verification at 40 Gbit/s is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Particle acceleration using the Vulcan Petawatt laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Using the upgraded Vulcan Petawatt laser at 3/spl times/10/sup 20/ Wcm/sup -2/ intensities, target interactions and acceleration in a gas jet were studied. Electron spectra with energies up to 240 MeV were detected. Indications of a new acceleration regime, which results in a nonMaxwellian distribution were observed.

abstract: 0.5 mm thick flux grown KTiOPO/sub 4/ has been poled with 800 nm domain period by employing electron-beam lithography and electric field poling. The structures can be used as an electrically amplitude adjustable Bragg reflector.

articleTitle: All-integrated Brillouin fiber ring laser using holey fiber
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An all-fiber Brillouin ring laser has been developed based on a /spl sim/100-m-long, 2.3-/spl mu/m-core-diameter holey fiber. The laser spectrum consisted of two interleaved counter-propagating combs of Stokes/anti-Stokes components that were separately extracted in a coupler.

articleTitle: Fabrication of periodical poling in 3mm-thick MgO:LiNbO/sub 3/ crystals at elevated temperature
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Temperature dependence of coercive field was investigated in MgO-doped LiNbO/sub 3/ and the field was found to be reduced to 1.2 kV/mm at 25/spl deg/C. Periodical structures with 30 /spl mu/m period was fabricated in 3 mm-thick MgO-doped LiNbO/sub 3/.

articleTitle: Frequency stability of a self-phase-locked degenerate continuous-wave optical parametric oscillator
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The properties of a self-phase-locked by-2-divider optical parametric oscillator are presented. A locking range of up to 156 MHz is measured, and the divider's relative frequency stability is shown to be better than 6/spl times/10/sup -14/.

articleTitle: Wafer scale profiling of photonic integrated circuits
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate a thermal profiling technique for wafer-scale testing of optical distribution in photonic integrated circuits. The technique is used to quantify the absorption coefficient of a subthreshold diode laser for varying operating conditions.

abstract: We analyze the gain flatness of Raman amplifiers using equally spaced pumps. We show that using an optimized central pump wavelength with equal pump spacing provides ample gain flatness and may simplify system design.

abstract: Over the past 15 years, there has been rapid progress in producing high peak power, ultrashort laser pulses by incorporating the technique of chirped pulse amplification (CPA). In this paper a laboratory-scaled PW Ti:sapphire laser system which is currently being produced 32.9-fs pulses with a peak power of 0.85-PW is investigated.

articleTitle: A high power, continuous wave, continuous tunable, narrow linewidth infrared OPO beyond 4 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We present two new continuous-wave OPOs, using continuously tunable high-power single-frequency pump lasers. We extended the operation of PPLN OPO's to 4.7 micrometer and we reached a stabilized single-frequency idler output power of 3 Watts.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A highly nonlinear 50 m long photonic crystal fibre with zero-dispersion wavelength at 1552 nm is investigated as a 40 to 10 Gb/s demultiplexer in a complete transmission system. 160 to 10 Gb/s is feasible.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Concepts, measurement, and reconstruction techniques for the wavefront of optical beams are considered. The significance of the wavefront is discussed in terms of correctability, beam-propagation, and quality, for increasing levels of complexity, reaching from the geometric optical approximation to the scalar theory of partial coherent beams. Experimental results are presented for the Hartmann-Shack sensor.

articleTitle: Optical MEMS fabrication, scaling and design of microoptical devices and systems
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: MEMS technology offer substantial advantages for optical systems: Tight dimensional tolerances allow accurate control of optical fields, MEMS actuators provide tunability, parallel processing leads to low cost, and miniaturization simplifies packaging and installation. Cost-effective use of microfabrication technology requires miniaturization, however, so optical MEMS presents unique challenges in design and scaling.

abstract: In this tutorial, the different techniques for optical 2R/3R regeneration targeting either ultra long-haul transmission and/or terrestrial networking applications at 40 Gbit/s will be reviewed. Principles of operation as well as recent system demonstrations will be described, highlighting the key features and potential applications of each and every approaches.

articleTitle: Raman amplifiers and fiber lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The summary form only given. Stimulated Raman scattering (SRS) is a process by which energy is transferred from one wavelength to the next through a nonlinear scattering process. This phenomenon can be used to Raman amplify signals in a telecommunication systems. In this tutorial, the process of SRS is reviewed; and the advantages of Raman pumping a transmission span, improved noise figure and gain flatness, are discussed. Problems that can arise such as, multiple path interference of Rayleigh backscattered light, and pump noise transfer are examined. Finally, pumping schemes such as multiple order Raman pumping and time division multiplexed pumping are studied.

articleTitle: Femtosecond laser micromachining of submicron features
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The summary form is given. Femtosecond laser micromachining of variety of materials has been pursued by several research groups for possible improvements due to the extremely short pulse width of the laser. We have used a Spectra Physics 2 mJ laser to explore the micromachining at submicron dimensions. The laser wavelength was 800 nm and was frequency doubled using a LBO crystal. An almost gaussian beam was obtained when the 400 nm wavelength light beam was spatially filtered using a pair of lens and a pinhole. The beam was focused using a microscope objective of 0.85 numerical aperture. The laser beam was scanned on a silicon wafer that was placed on a computer controlled x-y stage. The experiments were conducted in atmospheric air. The laser micromachined wafer was examined using an atomic force microscope (AFM). The laser marked line widths of 390 nm and depth of 200 nm were achieved with optimization of focus position, laser power and scan speed. AFM surface scan of a micromachined line on <100> silicon wafer is viewed. The results of laser beam shape, power, scan speed on micromachined line width; depth, rim formation and debris generation will be discussed. Spectroscopic measurements of the plasma generated during laser ablation process were performed. The achievement of submicron features allows the fabrication of various types of MEMS and optoelectronic devices for sensor and other applications using direct laser writing process.

articleTitle: Adaptive laser resonators
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Beam quality and output power of high-power solid state lasers were frequently limited by aberrations of the active medium. If a resonators were set up such that it forces the laser to operate in the TEM/sub 00/ fundamental transverse mode, aberrations cause high diffraction losses. This in turn leads to a strong reduction of the output power. In this paper, optical layout of master-oscillator-power-amplifier (MOPA) systems with adaptive aberration compensation was discussed. The genetic control algorithm was employed to control the deformable mirror and experimental results for the MOPA system was presented. For both systems commercial lamp-pumped Nd:YAG laser heads that can provide about 500 W of output power when used in a multimode resonator was used.

articleTitle: A novel approach towards two-photon absorption based detectors
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The summary form only given. We have demonstrated that the inherent inefficiency of the TPA process in semiconductors can be overcome by incorporating the semiconductor in a microcavity structure. Proof of concept devices with a 0.27/spl mu/m Ga/sub 0.7/Al0.3As active region and two Bragg reflectors with the cavity resonance of 890 nm were fabricated. We measured the TPA photocurrent of these devices and have demonstrated a factor of 12000 enhancement over a nonmicrocavity device at 890 nm. Our active length of 0.27 nm is as efficient as 5.4 mm without a microcavity, overcoming the very long detector lengths limiting the use of TPA in practical autocorrelators, optical switches and sampling devices for real telecommunication systems. The effect of the cavity is to enhance the intra-cavity optical intensity, which leads to an increase in the nonlinear response of the active region. We studied, theoretically and experimentally, the impact of the cavity on the temporal response and the sensitivity of the device, which are critical considerations for commercial applications. This cavity design has a 3 pico-second response time and the autocorrelation trace is comparable with the BBO crystal response for an input 1.6 ps pulse. Devices designed for 1550 nm have also been realised and our measurements indicate these two-photon absorption based detectors are potential candidates for optical autocorrelation of short optical pulses, and for optical switching and sampling in optical time division multiplexed (OTDM) communications systems.

abstract: We demonstrate OPO using periodically-poled MgO-doped near-stoichiometric LiTaO/sub 3/. The tuning ranges of signal and idler waves were 1.53 -1.63 /spl mu/m and 3.06-3.49 /spl mu/m, respectively. We obtained 65% slope efficiency and the maximum output power of 628 mW at 1.1 W pumping.

articleTitle: Recompression of short pulses stretched by fiber Bragg gratings
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Short pulses stretched by chirped fiber Bragg gratings and recompressed with standard bulk diffraction gratings based are experimentally characterised. The recompressed pulse duration is very close to its initial value.

articleTitle: Frequency converters in the midinfrared spectral region with periodically poled RbTiOPO/sub 4/
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: OPO's employing PPRTP operating in the spectral region of 1.55 /spl mu/m-3.4 /spl mu/m are demonstrated. Signal energies of 0.96 mJ are generated with a total OPO efficiency reaching 40% in a 11 mm-long crystal. Effective nonlinearity in PPRTP is 9 pm/V.

articleTitle: Broadly tunable external-cavity semiconductor lasers in optical-communication band using Fabry-Perot laser diodes without antireflection coating
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Using proper quantum-well structure, carriers distribute over a broad bandwidth, suppressing self-oscillation of uncoated Fabry-Perot laser diodes, but still providing gain for external-cavity configuration. Then broadband tuning range of 200 nm is achieved.

abstract: A gain clamped SOA combined with a distributed Raman fiber amplifier has a gain of 19.6 dB and a noise figure of 2.9 dB. Sixteen channels of 10 Gb/s signals are successfully transmitted over 5 spans of 80 km even under dynamic add-drop situations.

abstract: 4 W of laser power at 1040 nm has been achieved for the first time from an Yb-doped double clad PCF. The inner cladding of this fibre has the highest NA yet reported of 0.7-0.8.

abstract: A novel scheme of spot size converters is proposed and successfully demonstrated between high refractive index (4.0%) waveguides and conventional single mode fibers, whose coupling loss is evaluated to be 0.3 dB.

abstract: We investigate the transmission spectra in a single-mode fiber excited by two acoustic waves with orthogonal perturbations using a novel composite piezoelectric transducer. Polarization-dependent spectra are observed due to coherent acousto-optic coupling between core-to-cladding modes.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

articleTitle: Beam clean-up and combining via stimulated scattering in liquid crystals
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Orientational stimulated scattering from o-wave into e-wave in liquid crystal may combine coherent beams or modes of amplifiers) into diffraction-limited output. In experiment a 1000 micron liquid crystal layer transmitted undistorted o-wave with low attenuation.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We report a new label-free biosensor system for protein interaction characterization. The system consists of a VCSEL, a plastic guided mode resonant filter, and a pin detector. The sensor has high sensitivity and ultra compactness, consumes low power, and can be fabricated in 2D arrays.

articleTitle: Transmission over photonic crystal fiber at 40 Gbit/s using midspan spectral inversion in a highly photonic crystal fiber
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Transmission at 40 Gbit/s over large mode area photonic crystal fiber (PCF) together with dispersion compensation by optical phase conjugation in a highly nonlinear PCF are demonstrated for the first time.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An airbridge contacted quantum dot microdisk diode with continuous-wave lasing at 5 K is reported. The threshold current is as low as 43 /spl mu/A in 4 /spl mu/m diameter microdisks. Peak shifts indicate thermal heating of the structure.

articleTitle: 760 nm vertical cavity surface emitting lasers for gas sensing
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Lasing was observed for the first time for 766 nm vertical cavity surface emitting lasers with strained AlGaInAs/AlGaAs quantum wells. The selectively oxidized structure was grown by solid source molecular beam epitaxy and the lasers operated under pulsed excitation.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We report a pulsed singly-resonant OPO based on noncritically phase-matched ZGP with the lowest ever reported threshold of 2 /spl mu/J. The pump source was a 1-/spl mu/m-pumped PPLN OPO. Tuning its output from 2.3 to 3.7 /spl mu/m resulted in ZGP OPO tuning from 3.7 to 10.2 /spl mu/m.

Attenuation up to 20 times of transmitted beam was observed. Advantages of holographic filters in inorganic glass for laser power attenuation are discussed.

Alignment tolerances and experimental data are presented for two gratings using monochromatic light. Designs for broadband pulse compressions are discussed.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

articleTitle: Adaptive receivers for laser ultrasonics using photorefractive CdTe
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

abstract: This paper combines a resonant tunneling diode switched capacitor model of an electroabsorption modulator with standard Franz-Keldysh theory, explaining the measured device performance as the observed ratio of change in absorption coefficient to absorption coefficient.

abstract: Cascaded Raman Stokes lasing in a high-Q silica microsphere resonator is demonstrated. With less than 0.9 mW pump power, five cascaded Stokes lasing lines are generated. Stokes lasing lines exhibit distinct characteristics depending on their order.

abstract: We report an in-situ observation technique of twinning in crystal quartz and demonstrate periodic twins propagating in an anisotropic shape. The propagating direction was found to be parallel to the Y axis, which is different from the previous reports.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The feature size made by two-photon photopolymerization is described by a threshold model. In a negative photoresist SU-8 we show the linewidth fabricated by this nonlinear process is consistent with the prediction of this model.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The effect of strain in laser diodes with pyramidal quantum dots has been experimentally studied and theoretically modelled. Strongly polarised injection luminescence with extinction ratios as high as 18 dB is observed even at 1% threshold current.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

The multimode output beam is converted to singlemode by a two wave mixing process in an infrared sensitive photorefractive crystal. Up to 1 W singlemode output is achieved by compensation of thermally-induced phase fluctuations in the fiber.

abstract: We demonstrate a Raman laser integrated onto a silicon microchip, using an ultra-high-Q toroidal microcavity. Low pump power thresholds (210 microwatts) and Raman output powers of 1.2 milliWatts were obtained at 1650 nm.

articleTitle: Simultaneous measurement of angular and spectral properties of light scattering for early cancer detection
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: A novel instrument has been developed for the angular, spectral, azimuthal and polarization measurements of the light backscattering by living biological tissues. These measurements provide the most comprehensive quantitative information about the light scattering and allow obtaining unique quantitative information about the microarchitecture of living cells and tissues. We have shown the potential of this technique to characterize and diagnose very early premalignant changes in the epithelia, for which no histological or molecular markers has yet been established. Using this technique in our studies with a rodent model of colon carcinogenesis we obtained several parameters diagnostically significant for the detection of precancerous changes, such as the number density of red blood cells in the capillary network immediately underlying the epithelium, the fractal dimension of the tissue microarchitecture, and the average roundness of subcellular structures.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

articleTitle: Direct frequency comb generation from an octave spanning prismless Ti:sapphire laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An octave spanning prismless Ti:sapphire laser is demonstrated. The octave is reached at 20 dB below the average power level. A highly stable carrier-envelope beat note with 30 dB signal to noise in a 100 kHz detection bandwidth is observed.

articleTitle: Femtosecond pulses in the mid-infrared: generation, characterization and applications in condensed matter research
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Summary form only given. This tutorial combines a review of recent developments in pulse generation and characterization at wavelengths from 2.5 to 25 /spl mu/m (0.5 to 0.05 eV) with a discussion of spectroscopic methods for condensed matter research. Different sources of ultrashort mid-infrared pulses are described with the main emphasis on parametric frequency mixing. The state of the art in pulse shaping and phase-resolved pulse characterization in the mid-infrared will be presented and complemented by a discussion of spectroscopic methods, in particular multidimensional spectroscopies. The potential of such methods is illustrated by key applications in ultrafast semiconductor optics and vibrational spectroscopy of liquid systems.

abstract: We demonstrate stable multiGHz rate picosecond pulse generation by passive mode-locking of an extended cavity VCSEL which incorporates a saturable Bragg reflector mirror into a device, designed here as a high power 980 nm InGaAs multiple quantum-well vertical cavity source.

Pulses as short as 94-fs have been obtained at 1070 nm with an average power of 110 mW. We also discussed the first results obtained with this crystal in a regenerative amplifier cavity.

articleTitle: Vacuum-ultraviolet laser nano-milling of surface-relief gratings on optical fiber ends
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

The noninteger intensity dependence is explained by a model including defect density fluctuations and nonlinear carrier transport phenomena.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Refractive index changes in intensively-pumped Nd:YAG crystals were studied using both polarization interferometer and transient grating method. publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Simultaneous laser emission at wavelengths 8.6 and 10.4/spl mu/m is reported for a GaAs based quantum cascade laser. These devices are an ideal compact source for frequency mixing applications over the mid/far infrared.

articleTitle: The analysis of polarization in a nonplanar ring laser
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The study of polarization evolution in a nonplanar ring cavity is presented. The thermally induced optic axis rotation in the gain medium and the thermal-dependent dielectric tensor are determined which enables Jones matrix analysis on polarization in the ring cavity.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Nonlinear optical measurements play an important role in characterization of colloidal solution. It is necessary to design a method for fast, simple and in the same time accurate nonlinear optical characterization of solutions. This paper describes a simple method to measure third-order nonlinear susceptibilities of highly scattered liquids. This method is currently applied for studying the aggregation and polarization of nanoparticles and microspheres in solution.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We have observed periodical movement of the crystal LiNbO/sub 3/:Fe (mass is 0.47 g) actuated by solid state CW laser. Oscillations with angular amplitude up to 0.6/spl deg/ were detected using capacitor type arrangement.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We describe the first demonstration of self-channeling in the atmosphere by bursts of high power femtosecond laser pulses. We study the long distance energy propagation and ablation of solid targets by the self-channeled beam.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We present a novel holographic wavelength filter that is based on interband photorefraction. we use an acousto-optic deflector to control the direction of the recording beams and the spacing of the UV induced photorefractive grating. publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

abstract: A method for improving the resolution of a lithographic system by an arbitrary amount (with no visibility reduction for incoherent mask methods) is proposed and demonstrated experimentally. The method simply relies on the sharpened features available through N-photon detection.

abstract: We have measured the spectral linewidth of a terahertz-frequency quantum cascade laser by using a GaAs diode mixer and heterodyning with two far-infrared gas lasers. Current-tuning characteristics of the laser are also reported.

abstract: Due to its noninvasive nature and submicrometer 3-D sectioning power, harmonic generation microscopies is most suitable in studying vertebrate morphogenesis in vivo with no need of extrinsic or intrinsic fluorophores.

abstract: Ultrahigh axial resolution OCT and enhanced penetration in highly scattering media is demonstrated with two fiber broadened femtosecond light sources, operating in the visible and in the near infrared in human cells and other human biopsies.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Crystallinity of CLBO could be drastically improved by solution-stirring method. They possessed high bulk and surface laser-induced damage thresholds, and the qualities were adequately uniform throughout the crystals. 40-W UV output was obtained by using these high-quality uniform crystals.

abstract: Using image processing, we achieve spatial resolution enhancement for a coherent, synthetic, phased-array THz imaging system. These techniques eliminate higher order scattering processes, or clutter, and recover otherwise lost resolution in images of two abutting 397 /spl mu/m diameter spheres.

articleTitle: Wavelength dependent damage threshold measurements to determine initiation mechanisms
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The laser damage threshold of KD/sub 2/PO/sub 4/, a 7.2 eV dielectric, is measured as a function of wavelength. Steps in the damage threshold at photon energies near fractions of the band gap suggesting defect assisted multiphoton damage initiation.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Mode-locking of the Yb:Sc/sub 2/O/sub 3/ laser with a saturable absorber mirror is demonstrated. The pump efficiency reached 47% in the picosecond regime and with dispersion compensation pulses as short as 230 fs were obtained at 1044.5 nm.

articleTitle: Design and performance of AlGaAsSb/InGaAsSb/GaSb type-I quantum well diode lasers
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: This paper presents the design and performance of antimonide-based, type-I, quantum-well diode lasers. Using 1.5-% compressively strained InGaAsSb quantum wells, the quaternary's miscibility gap was avoided to produce room-temperature devices emitting at 2.5 and 2.8 /spl mu/m. The 2.5-/spl mu/m devices output 1 W continuous wave and nearly 5 W in pulsed operation. Modal gain measurements show internal losses less than 4 cm/sup -1/. This design should produce room-temperature diode lasers with wavelengths greater than 3 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: F/sub 2/-laser micromachining of microfluidic channels and vias for biophotonic chip applications
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Deep-ultraviolet F/sub 2/-laser radiation drives strong interactions in optically transparent glasses for smooth and crack-free shaping of microfluidic channels, microvias, and arrays for cell-on-a-chip applications. We describe cell manipulation and imaging applications in custom fabricated biophotonic chips.

articleTitle: Spectral broadening of 50 fs Cr:YAG pulses around 1.5 /spl mu/m in the tapered fiber
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The spectral broadening of the 50 femtosecond pulses from the Cr:YAG laser at 1.5 /spl mu/m in a tapered fiber with 1.4 /spl mu/m taper waist diameter is observed. The broadening mechanism around the second dispersion zero is studied experimentally and numerically.

articleTitle: THz waveguides for efficient THz parametric conversion
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We have considered slab and rib waveguides for THz waves to improve the efficiency' for THz parametric conversion. We show that for a quasi-single-mode slab waveguide, periodic poling is no longer necessary for achieving phase matching.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The visibility of the interference pattern of a Mach-Zehnder-interferometer is investigated in dependence of the spatial coherence. It is demonstrated how the dimensions of the fringe pattern can be shortened significantly due to the low coherence properties. Applications of spatial high resolved velocity measurements in fluid flows are given.

articleTitle: Low-PDG Raman amplification via 10 GHz polarization sweeping with LiNbO/sub 3/ phase modulator
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We propose and demonstrate a novel scheme to achieve low polarization dependent gain (PDG) forward-pumped Raman amplification via polarization sweeping at 10 GHz. This scheme employs the asymmetry of electro-optic coefficients of LiNbO/sub 3/ crystals to sweep the pump SOP at 10 GHz across the Poincare sphere.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: The decay of N=2 solitons, initiated by a step dispersion change, is shown to form stable pulse pairs whose wavelengths are shifted to either side of the input wavelength. Partial soliton recovery is also demonstrated.

articleTitle: Continuous wave operation of a quantum-cascade laser emitting near 5.6 /spl mu/m
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Continuous wave operation at -30/spl deg/ C of buried heterostructure quantum cascade laser emitting at 5.64 um is reported. The laser exhibited 3 mW of CW power with the threshold current density of 5.4 kA/cm/sup 2/.

abstract: Nearly-complete mode-selective coupling from an optical fiber taper to a photonic crystal defect waveguide is demonstrated experimentally. We observe 95% power transfer with a 20 nm bandwidth and a coupling length less then 65 /spl mu/m.

articleTitle: In vivo spectral transmission measurements through single and multiple tissue layers and blood
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An in vivo animal model study of the optical properties and light transmission characteristics of single and multiple tissue layers and blood using either coherent or incoherent light sources in a broad spectral range covering the visible and near-infrared is presented.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We demonstrate the ability of polarization spectroscopy and elastography, in conjunction with optical coherence tomography, to determine the properties of collagen organization in musculoskeletal tissue. Optical coherence tomography images correlated with histologic analysis of collagen.

abstract: Two dimensional electro-optic sampling allows a target's scattered terahertz field to be measured. By obtaining multiple projection images we have performed the reconstruction of three dimensional targets with millimeter resolution.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We show experimentally that the optical nonlinearities due to intersubband transitions in GaN quantum wells can have both signs, depending on the structure of choice. Nonlinear transmission measurements show strong, ultrafast induced absorption that may be used in future nonlinear optical devices.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: An autocorrelator-like set up is proposed to characterize optical nonlinear effects in a photodiode. Experimental results are confronted with theoretical analysis at second and third orders, justifying two photon absorption use in auto-correlators.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.

The experiments used an uncoated gain chip with TE-stabilization from -46 to 0/spl deg/C. The chip was used in a Littman-Metcalf cavity. A combination of coarse grating tuning and fine phase tuning allows continuous wavelength tuning in pulsed, uncoated QC lasers.

articleTitle: Sub-Doppler atomic vapor photon detection via electromagnetically induced transparency
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: High spectral resolution photon detection has been achieved by exploiting the narrow absorption features of gas phase atoms. Velocity-selective excitation and coherent optical effects have allowed for increased spectral discrimination and laser Doppler velocimetry.

abstract: We present comparative measurements of polarization dependent gain in neodymium and ytterbium doped fiber amplifiers. We demonstrate, that this effect is always present in neodymium doped amplifiers while it can be suppressed in ytterbium doped amplifiers.

articleTitle: Crystal structures within optical tweezers

abstract: We create microcrystal structures using holographic optical tweezers to position and hold objects in three dimensions. The structures can be scaled or rotated about arbitrary axes, or made permanent by gelling the surrounding fluid.

abstract: The light dynamics in ray optics limit corresponding to asymmetric particles is generally chaotic, which changes scattering modes directionality pattern and lifetime distribution. We develop the analytical theory to find scattering properties of the asymmetric particles. Our analytical results are in agreement with numerical simulations.

abstract: Recent advances in the generation of attosecond-duration electromagnetic pulses demand the development of methods to measure them. The combination of sources and measurement technology provides an important set of tools for the study of electron dynamics in matter of all kinds. I survey several recent proposals for attoseconds metrology, and compare their efficacy and range of applicability.

abstract: Fresnel lenses have a number of attractive properties for pulsed terahertz imaging. We demonstrate tomographic imaging with a Fresnel lens and report progress towards the goal of long range terahertz imaging.

publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We overview how the novel electronic structure of dilute nitride alloys modifies the gain characteristics of GaInNAs lasers. Optimised devices should have comparable or better characteristics than InP-based emitters, enabling GaAs-based 1.3 /spl mu/m vertical emitting lasers.

articleTitle: Enhanced Raman gain of novel bulk glasses

articleTitle: X-ray radiation from nonlinear Thomson scattering of an intense femtosecond laser focussed in an helium gas jet
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: We have observed the X-ray radiation produced by the nonlinear Thomson scattering of an intense femtosecond laser on relativistic electrons. The 1 J 30 fs laser beam is focussed on a helium gas jet and the X-ray radiation is detected using a grazing incidence X-ray spectrometer. The analysis of the data shows that the effect of the plasma as well as the additional acceleration of the electrons inside the plasma waves should be taken into account to fit the experimental results.

articleTitle: Oximetry of tissue vasculature with near infrared spectroscopy: application to tumors
publicationTitle: Conference on Lasers and Electro-Optics, 2003. CLEO '03.
abstract: Near infrared (NIR) spectroscopy has been demonstrated as a new means to quantify oxygenation of tissue vasculature, in particular changes in hemoglobin concentrations and oxygen saturation. A novel application such oximetry to monitoring of tumor vascular oxygenation during respiratory interventions will be presented. Our recent results obtained with a one-channel NIR spectrometer observing rat breast and prostate tumors in vivo have demonstrated a biphasic response of tumor vascular oxygenation when the inhaled gas is switched from air to carbogen. We present a mathematical model associating the tumor vascular oxygenation to both well-perfused and poorly perfused regions in the tumor. Furthermore, laboratory phantom experiments and computational simulations using the finite element method have been conducted to verify this tumor hemodynamic model.
